arxiv-1811-09837.title: Identification of Treatment Effects under Limited Exogenous Variation Thanks: † Department of Economics, MIT Thanks: § \lx@sectionsign Department of Economics, University of Bristol and University of Melbourne Thanks: We are grateful to Jean-Pierre Florens, Michal Kolesár, Martin Weidner, Frank Wind
arxiv-1811-09837.creator: Whitney K. Newey † and Sami Stouli §
arxiv-1811-09837.description: Abstract . Multidimensional heterogeneity and endogeneity are important features of a wide class of econometric models. With control variables to correct for endogeneity, nonparametric identification of treatment effects requires strong support conditions. To alleviate this requirement, we consider varying coefficients specifications for the conditional expectation function of the outcome given a treatment and control variables.

arxiv-1909-07521.title: Probing Natural Language Inference Models through Semantic Fragments
arxiv-1909-07521.creator: Kyle Richardson and Hai Hu and Lawrence S. Moss and Ashish Sabharwal
arxiv-1909-07521.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Kyle Richardson and Hai Hu and Lawrence S. Moss and Ashish Sabharwal. Do state-of-the-art models for language understanding already have, or can they easily learn, abilities such as boolean coordination, quantification, conditionals, comparatives, and monotonicity reasoning (i.e., reasoning about word substitutions in sentential contexts)? While such phenomena are involved in natural language inference (NLI) and go beyond basic linguistic understanding, it is unclear the extent to which they are captured in existing NLI benchmarks and effectively learned by models.

arxiv-2006-14988.title: Unlabelled Data Improves Bayesian Uncertainty Calibration under Covariate Shift
arxiv-2006-14988.creator: Alex J. Chan, Ahmed M. Alaa, Zhaozhi Qian, Mihaela van der Schaar
arxiv-2006-14988.description: Abstract Modern neural networks have proven to be powerful function approximators, providing state-of-the-art performance in a multitude of applications. They however fall short in their ability to quantify confidence in their predictions — this is crucial in high-stakes applications that involve critical decision-making.

arxiv-2101-02602.title: Schemes in Lean Thanks: The first author was supported in part by EPSRC grant EP/L025485/1.
arxiv-2101-02602.creator: Kevin Buzzard, Chris Hughes, Kenny Lau, Amelia Livingston, Ramon Fernández Mir, Scott Morrison
arxiv-2101-02602.description: Abstract . We tell the story of how schemes were formalised in three different ways in the Lean theorem prover. 1. Introduction and overview 1.1. Varieties and schemes in algebraic geometry Before 1960, algebraic geometry was done via the theory of algebraic varieties, finite-dimensional objects defined over a fixed algebraically closed field, or “universal domain”.

arxiv-2101-05287.title: A general quantum algorithm for open quantum dynamics demonstrated with the Fenna-Matthews-Olson complex
arxiv-2101-05287.creator: Zixuan Hu, Kade Head-Marsden, David A. Mazziotti, Prineha Narang, Sabre Kais
arxiv-2101-05287.description: Abstract Using quantum algorithms to simulate complex physical processes and correlations in quantum matter has been a major direction of quantum computing research, towards the promise of a quantum advantage over classical approaches. In this work we develop a generalized quantum algorithm to simulate any dynamical process represented by either the operator sum representation or the Lindblad master equation.

arxiv-2106-06182.title: Wigner symmetries and Gleason’s theorem Thanks: This research was supported by grants P1-0288 and J1-2454 from ARRS, Slovenia.
arxiv-2106-06182.creator: Peter Šemrl
arxiv-2106-06182.description: Abstract We prove an optimal version of Uhlhorn’s generalization of Wigner’s unitary-antiunitary theorem. The main tool in our proof is Gleason’s theorem. AMS classification: 81P10, 81R15. Keywords: Symmetry; Gleason’s theorem. 1 Introduction and statement of the main results Let H ba a finite or infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.

arxiv-2205-08852.creator: Tanjila Mawla, Maanak Gupta, Ravi Sandhu
arxiv-2205-08852.description: Abstract . Cyber physical ecosystem connects different intelligent devices over heterogeneous networks. Various operations are performed on smart objects to ensure efficiency and to support automation in smart environments. An Activity (defined by Gupta and Sandhu ( Gupta and Sandhu 2021 ) ) reflects the current state of an object, which changes in response to requested operations.

arxiv-2306-04692.creator: Ulrich P. Steinwandel, Klaus Dolag, Ludwig M. Böss, Tirso Marin-Gilabert
arxiv-2306-04692.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ulrich P. Steinwandel, Klaus Dolag, Ludwig M. Böss, Tirso Marin-Gilabert. We present the first results of one extremely high resolution, non-radiative magnetohydrodynamical cosmological zoom-in simulation of a massive cluster with a virial mass M vir = 2.0 × 10 15 {}_{\mathrm{vir}}=2.0\times 10^{15} solar masses. We adopt a mass resolution of 4 × 10 5 4\times 10^{5} M ⊙ with a maximum spatial resolution of around 250 pc in the central regions of the cluster.

arxiv-2306-14815.title: Analysis of Boolean Functions Related to Binary Input Binary Output Two-party Nonlocal Games
arxiv-2306-14815.creator: Jyotirmoy Basak, Subhamoy Maitra, Prabal Paul, Animesh Roy
arxiv-2306-14815.description: Abstract The famous CHSH game can be interpreted with Boolean functions while understanding the success probability in the classical scenario. In this paper, we have exhaustively studied all the Boolean functions on four variables to express binary input binary output two-party nonlocal games and explore their performance in both classical and quantum scenarios.

arxiv-2409-14697.title: QueenV2: Future of Quantum Circuit Simulation Seven Seas of Rhye
arxiv-2409-14697.creator: Chuan-Chi Wang
arxiv-2409-14697.description: Abstract A state vector-based quantum circuit simulation can provide accurate results for the development and validation of quantum computing algorithms, without being affected by noise interference. However, existing quantum circuit simulators have consistently underperformed due to inadequate integration with quantum circuits and high-performance computing architectures.

arxiv-2411-13732.title: Typing Composite Subjects
arxiv-2411-13732.creator: Luca Aceto, Daniele Gorla, Stian Lybech 0
arxiv-2411-13732.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Luca Aceto, Daniele Gorla, Stian Lybech 0. 1
Introduction

Process calculi are formalisms for modelling and reasoning about concurrent and distributed programs, and one way of reasoning about the safety of such programs is by means of
type systems
. In that approach, types are usually assigned to atomic identifiers, such as variables, function names and, in the case of process calculi with communication primitives, to
channel names
.

arxiv-2503-14944.title: MMAIF: Multi-task and Multi-degradation All-in-One for Image Fusion with Language Guidance
arxiv-2503-14944.creator: Zihan Cao, Yu Zhong, Ziqi Wang, Liang-Jian Deng
arxiv-2503-14944.description: Abstract Image fusion, a fundamental low-level vision task, aims to integrate multiple image sequences into a single output while preserving as much information as possible from the input. However, existing methods face several significant limitations: 1) requiring task- or dataset-specific models; 2) neglecting real-world image degradations ( e.g.

arxiv-2507-09032.title: Modeling Latent Underdispersion with Discrete Order Statistics
arxiv-2507-09032.creator: Jimmy Lederman, Aaron Schein
arxiv-2507-09032.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jimmy Lederman, Aaron Schein. The Poisson distribution is the default choice of likelihood for probabilistic models of count data. However, due to the equidispersion contraint of the Poisson, such models may have predictive uncertainty that is artificially inflated. While overdispersion has been extensively studied, conditional underdispersion—where latent structure renders data more regular than Poisson—remains underexplored, in part due to the lack of tractable modeling tools.

arxiv-2508-14002.title: Chiral effective potential in 4 ​ D , 𝒩 = 1 4D,\,\mathcal{N}=1 supersymmetric gauge theories
arxiv-2508-14002.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . We calculate the chiral effective superpotential in 4 ​ D 4D 𝒩 = 1 , S ​ U ​ ( N ) \mathcal{N}=1,\,SU(N) super Yang-Mills theory coupled to chiral matter in one- and two-loop approximations. It is found that the one-loop contribution to the chiral effective potential is always finite and is expressed in terms of a specific triangle integral. The two-loop contributions generated by purely chiral vertices turned out to be finite as well.

arxiv-2509-09463.title: Minimality of Tree Tensor Network Ranks
arxiv-2509-09463.creator: Jana Jovcheva, Tim Seynnaeve, Nick Vannieuwenhoven
arxiv-2509-09463.description: Abstract . For a given tree tensor network G G , we call a tuple of bond dimensions minimal if there exists a tensor T T that can be represented by this network but not on the same tree topology with strictly smaller bond dimensions.

plos-pone-0001081.description: PLOS ONE research article. Plants defend themselves against herbivorous insects, utilizing both constitutive and inducible defenses. Induced defenses are controlled by several phytohormone-mediated signaling pathways. Here, we analyze transcriptional changes in the North American Arabidopsis relative Boech

plos-pone-0008415.creator: Paul A. Baldock, Nicola J. Lee, Frank Driessler et al.
plos-pone-0008415.description: PLOS ONE research article. Changes in whole body energy levels are closely linked to alterations in body weight and bone mass. Here, we show that hypothalamic signals contribute to the regulation of bone mass in a manner consistent with the central perception of energy status. Mice lacking neuropeptide Y (

plos-pone-0011941.title: Phage-Derived Fully Human Monoclonal Antibody Fragments to Human Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-C Block Its Interaction with VEGF Receptor-2 and 3
plos-pone-0011941.creator: Matthias Rinderknecht, Alessandra Villa, Kurt Ballmer-Hofer et al.
plos-pone-0011941.description: PLOS ONE research article. Vascular endothelial growth factor C (VEGF-C) is a key mediator of lymphangiogenesis, acting via its receptors VEGF-R2 and VEGF-R3. High expression of VEGF-C in tumors correlates with increased lymphatic vessel density, lymphatic vessel invasion, sentinel lymph node metastasis an

plos-pone-0357999.title: Bacterial RNA downregulates MHC-I in tumor cell lines, promoting NK response and delaying tumor growth
plos-pone-0357999.creator: Agustina Serafino, Mónica Vermeulen, Yasmín A Bertinat, Federico Birnberg-Weiss, Joselyn E Castro, María Belén Bordignon, Ayelén I Pesce Viglietti, Jorgelina Bueno

pmc-10578914.title: Tissue-specific differences in the assembly of mitochondrial Complex I are revealed by a novel ENU mutation in ECSIT
pmc-10578914.creator: Thomas Nicol, Sara Falcone, Andrew Blease, Pratik Vikhe, Gabriele Civiletto, Saleh Salman Omairi, Carlo Viscomi, Ketan Patel, Paul K Potter
pmc-10578914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). AimsMitochondrial Complex I assembly (MCIA) is a multi-step process that necessitates the involvement of a variety of assembly factors and chaperones to ensure that the final active enzyme is correctly assembled. The role of the assembly factor evolutionarily conserved signalling intermediate in the toll (ECSIT) pathway was studied across various murine tissues to determine its role in this process and how this varied between tissues of varying energetic demands.

pmc-10591630.title: P048 Does Sleep Reduce Intrusive Memories after Analogue Trauma? Recent findings of Experimental Sleep Manipulations using the Trauma Film Paradigm
pmc-10591630.creator: J Ogden, L Jobson, S Drummond
pmc-10591630.description: IntroductionIntrusive memories are common in the aftermath of trauma, and these can develop into a pervasive, distressing symptom of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Sleep disturbances have also been shown to contribute to later development and maintenance of overall PTSD symptoms. Recent evidence suggests there is a relationship between sleep disturbance and intrusive memories following experimental analogue trauma.

pmc-10595793.title: Subjective and Objective Evaluation of Driving Behaviour in Depression
pmc-10595793.creator: V Tsoutsi, M Papadakaki, G Yannis, D Pavlou, M Basta, J Chliaoutakis, D Dikeos
pmc-10595793.description: IntroductionRoad traffic collisions and related casualties are a major issue for public health and society. Depression is characterized by mental, emotional and executive dysfunction, which may have an impact on driving behaviour. Among its symptoms sleep disturbance is very common.

pmc-10707015.title: Vitamin A, D, E, and K as Matrix Metalloproteinase-2/9 Regulators That Affect Expression and Enzymatic Activity
pmc-10707015.creator: Ha Vy Thi Vo, Yen Thi Nguyen, Namdoo Kim, Hyuck Jin Lee, Anargyros N Moulas
pmc-10707015.description: Fat-soluble vitamins (vitamin A, D, E, and K) assume a pivotal role in maintaining human homeostasis by virtue of their enzymatic functions. The daily inclusion of these vitamins is imperative to the upkeep of various physiological processes including vision, bone health, immunity, and protection against oxidative stress. Current research highlights fat-soluble vitamins as potential therapeutics for human diseases, especially cancer.

pmc-11293878.title: Three-dimensional matrix stiffness modulates mechanosensitive and phenotypic alterations in oral squamous cell carcinoma spheroids
pmc-11293878.creator: Maulee Sheth, Manju Sharma, Maria Lehn, HasanAl Reza, Takanori Takebe, Vinita Takiar, Trisha Wise-Draper, Leyla Esfandiari
pmc-11293878.description: Extracellular biophysical cues such as matrix stiffness are key stimuli tuning cell fate and affecting tumor progression in vivo. However, it remains unclear how cancer spheroids in a 3D microenvironment perceive matrix mechanical stiffness stimuli and translate them into intracellular signals driving progression.

pmc-11470398.title: Detection of COVID-19 incidence among attendees of the 2022 Hajj season
pmc-11470398.creator: Thamir A Alandijany, Fadi S Qashqari, Mohammad Alfelali, Sumyya H Hariri, Ahmed M Hassan, Arwa A Faizo, Yusuf M Khairo, Hanin A Qashqari, Elaf M Bahareth, Abdullah A Bajodah, Abdullah F Saeedi, Raed M Garout, Sherif A El-Kafrawy, Esam I Azhar
pmc-11470398.description: Highlights•Respiratory viral infections are of global concern during mass gatherings.•The nature of Hajj rituals offers a favorable environment for respiratory infections.•The number of COVID-19 cases in the last two Hajj seasons, 2022 and 2023, is unknown.•This study found few COVID-19 cases among 2022 Hajj attendees.•Continuous surveillance of respiratory viruses during Hajj seasons remain important.

pmc-12473491.title: A Method for Sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) Organ Segmentation and Phenotypic Parameter Extraction Based on CAVF-PointNet++
pmc-12473491.creator: Xinyuan Wei, Qiang Wang, Kaixuan Li, Wuping Zhang, Vittorio Rossi
pmc-12473491.description: Efficient and non-destructive extraction of organ-level phenotypic parameters of sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) plants is a key bottleneck in current sesame phenotyping research. To address this issue, this study proposes a method for organ segmentation and phenotypic parameter extraction based on CAVF-PointNet++ and geometric clustering. First, this method constructs a high-precision 3D point cloud using multi-view RGB image sequences.

pmc-12507712.title: When embodiment matters most: a confirmatory study on VR priming in motor imagery brain-computer interfaces training
pmc-12507712.creator: Daniela Esteves, Katarina Vagaja, Alexandre Andrade, Athanasios Vourvopoulos
pmc-12507712.description: BackgroundVirtual Reality (VR) feedback is increasingly integrated into Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications, enhancing the Sense of Embodiment (SoE) toward virtual avatars and fostering more vivid motor imagery (MI). VR-based MI-BCIs hold promise for motor rehabilitation, but their effectiveness depends on neurofeedback quality.

pmc-12572389.title: SCBM-Net: a multimodal feature fusion-based dual-channel method for bearing fault diagnosis
pmc-12572389.creator: Qiang Liu, Weiyan Tong, Hongwei Bai, Shien Dong
pmc-12572389.description: To address the limitations of single-modal approaches in bearing fault diagnosis under complex operating conditions, this study proposes SCBM-Net—a novel deep learning model based on a dual-channel multimodal fusion architecture. The model innovatively combines Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) to extract complementary features from time–frequency images and temporal signals, respectively.

pmc-12649579.title: Optimized 3D-Printed Polylactic Acid/Graphene Oxide Scaffolds for Enhanced Bone Regeneration
pmc-12649579.creator: Jung-Tae Lee, Dajung Lee, Ye-Seul Jung, Sung-Ho Lee, Sungtae Kim, Bongju Kim, Dong-Wook Han, Andreas Zenthöfer, Ralf Erber
pmc-12649579.description: Background: Three-dimensional (3D) printed scaffolds have emerged as promising tools for bone regeneration, but the optimal structural design and pore size remain unclear. Polylactic acid (PLA) reinforced with graphene oxide (GO) offers enhanced mechanical and biological performance, yet systematic evaluation of architecture and pore size is limited.

pmc-12700474.title: Incidence, causes, and effects of intraoperative hypothermia during elective oesophagectomy at a tertiary care centre- An observational study
pmc-12700474.creator: Swapnil Y Parab, Sargam Kant, Madhavi Shetmahajan, Priya Ranganathan
pmc-12700474.description: Background and Aims:Patients undergoing oesophagectomies are at risk of intraoperative hypothermia. The study aims to determine the incidence of hypothermia during oesophagectomy surgeries.Methods:This observational bidirectional study evaluated 266 adult patients (175 retrospective and 91 prospective) undergoing elective oesophagectomy at a tertiary care centre between 2019 and 2022. Intraoperative core temperature was monitored hourly using a nasopharyngeal probe.

pmc-13066489.title: Engineering NIR-II carbon dots through aniline extension with graphene and nitrogen enrichment for hepatobiliary theranostics
pmc-13066489.creator: Lijuan Yang, Man Li, Yisheng Peng, Yu Zhou, Junjie Zou, Huanhuan Liu, Wenxiang Zhang, Jie Liu, Peng He, Fan Dai, Jingwen Zheng, Jing Lin, Songnan Qu, Zhixiang Lu, Gang Liu
pmc-13066489.description: Near-infrared-II carbon dots offer exceptional deep-tissue penetration for biomedical imaging, but challenges remain in their synthesis and photoluminescence mechanisms. Here, we report three carbon dots (CDs-1, CDs-2, CDs-3) with tunable emission from the visible to the Near-infrared-II (480–1265 nm), synthesized by constructing extended aniline-based frameworks from p-phenylenediamine.

pmc-13259733.title: The mediating effect of arteriosclerosis on the relationship between sarcopenia and cognitive impairment: a retrospective analysis
pmc-13259733.creator: GangWei Zhang, YiJie Wang, DaoYuan Guo, Ci Lv, YuanYuan Du, XiaoMei Wang
pmc-13259733.description: ObjectiveSarcopenia and arteriosclerosis are important factors affecting cognitive function, but their interrelationships remain unclear. This study investigated whether arteriosclerosis mediates the mediation effect between sarcopenia and cognitive impairment.MethodsA total of 105 patients aged ≥ 60 years from geriatric clinics were enrolled. Sarcopenia was diagnosed according to the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria.

pmc-13404672.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids Attenuate Neuropathic Pain by Modulating Ferroptotic Stress, Selenoamino Acid Metabolism, and Lipid Remodeling
pmc-13404672.creator: Viet H. Dinh, Magda Descorbeth, Francis Zamora, Jo-Wen Liu, Cono Badalamenti, Salvador Soriano, Johnny D. Figueroa, Marino De León, Alfonso M. Durán
pmc-13404672.description: Neuropathic pain (NP) arises from diverse conditions, including peripheral nerve injury, spinal cord injury (SCI), and painful diabetic neuropathy, yet these disorders share oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid dysregulation, and altered neuronal excitability. We investigated whether dietary omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids modulate ferroptotic stress-associated pathways, defined as lipid peroxidation susceptibility and impaired antioxidant defense rather than overt ferroptotic cell death.

pmc-13656963.title: Lipoprotein(a) and the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index in relation to coronary lesion burden in patients with acute coronary syndrome
pmc-13656963.creator: Pinpeng Xie, Zhiyuan Wang, Chaosheng Huang, Wanting Sun, Weichun Zhu, Chungang Zhai, Lei Qiao, Wenqiang Chen
pmc-13656963.description: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] reflects inherited atherothrombotic risk, whereas the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) integrates systemic inflammation, triglyceride-related lipid disturbance, and glucose-related metabolic stress. Their individual and joint association with angiographic coronary lesion burden in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remain incompletely defined. We examined whether CTI complements Lp(a) in characterizing coronary lesion burden in ACS.

uslaw-usc-t36-s2307.title: 36 U.S.C. § 2307 — Gifts, bequests, and devises of property; tax treatment
uslaw-usc-t36-s2307.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s2307.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (United States Government Organizations Involved With Observances And Ceremonies); Chapter 23 (United States Holocaust Memorial Museum). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Museum may solicit, and the Museum may accept, hold, administer, invest, and use gifts, bequests, and devises of property, both real and personal, and all revenues.
